original.guitar: Jean Millaire (Marjo's guitarist and co-writer on the album)
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-80s Quebec rock: clean chorus for the verses, Marshall-style crunch for the choruses
original.effects: Chorus, stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: The big hit from Celle qui va (1986), Marjo's first solo album, recorded with Jean Millaire on Kébec-Disc.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the clean, chorused verses: switch to the middle position for a softer sound. Channel B for the rock choruses: JCM800-style crunch on the bridge humbucker. Stomp MOD off on channel B if the chorus makes the crunch too washy. For the solo, switch to CHATS SO.
recipes.why: Mid-80s rock ballads move from a clean, chorused verse to a crunchy chorus. A JCM800-style amp gives the punch of that era, with a stereo delay and a hall reverb for the big production.

original.guitar: Jean Millaire (Marjo's guitarist and co-writer on the album)
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-80s rock lead: Marshall-style crunch pushed by an overdrive
original.effects: Overdrive, stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: The big hit from Celle qui va (1986), Marjo's first solo album.

recipes.tips: Channel B for the solo: it loads on B, ready to play. Channel A is a slightly lower-gain version for lead lines. The stereo delay ducks under your playing and fills the gaps between phrases. Lots of vibrato and long bends suit the 80s rock style.
recipes.why: A JCM800-style amp pushed by a light overdrive gives the singing, sustained 80s rock lead. A long stereo delay and a hall reverb add the big production of the era.
